$comment: Purser-authored tests that are NOT executable, and why. scripts/run-purser-tests.mjs
reads this file, refuses to run the entries, and prints every one of them on each CI
run so a quarantined test can never be mistaken for a passing one.
This list exists because these files were authored but never executed by any runner —
tests/purser was outside jest's testMatch, so nothing here had ever run. Wiring the
directory into CI surfaced them all at once. A quarantined entry is a DEBT, not a
decision: fix the entry and delete it from this file.
An entry is only legitimate here if the TEST cannot run. A test that runs and FAILS
belongs in CI failing — that is the gate working. Do not quarantine a red test to get

quarantined.reason: UNSAFE: appends to tracked scripts/build-whitepapers.sh and website-v2/src/data/whitePapers.ts at repoRoot with no cleanup, dirtying the checkout for every later CI step. Its first assertion is also unsatisfiable — it edits a working-tree file and then asserts `git rev-parse HEAD` changed, which no file edit can do.
quarantined.fix: Run against an isolated fixture repo and restore mutated files in a finally block; replace the HEAD-moved assertion with one about the rebuild decision it actually means to test.

quarantined.reason: UNSAFE: runs `git commit --amend --date=...` with cwd tests/purser/rebase-test. That directory was never committed, which is the only reason the amend is currently inert. If anyone creates it as a plain directory inside this repo rather than a standalone `git init` sandbox, the amend rewrites port-daddy's real HEAD commit.
quarantined.fix: Create the fixture as an isolated `git init` sandbox outside the repo's worktree. Note the test's premise also appears inverted: build-whitepapers.sh exists because author time SURVIVES rebase, yet this asserts the epoch must change.

quarantined.reason: Fixture directories tests/purser/empty-repo and tests/purser/dependency-test were never committed by 1cad994, so the test dies on `cd`. It also invokes `./build-whitepapers.sh paper_epoch`, but paper_epoch is an internal bash function, not a subcommand — the argument parses as FILTER, matches no paper, and exits 0.
quarantined.fix: Commit the fixtures and call the epoch logic through a real entry point.

quarantined.reason: Fixture directories tests/purser/missing-sources and tests/purser/invalid-git were never committed, and the relative path ../scripts/build-whitepapers.sh would resolve to tests/purser/scripts/ regardless.
quarantined.fix: Commit the fixtures and correct the path. NOTE: this test is chasing a REAL defect — see paper-epoch-silent-fallback below.

quarantined.reason: ENVIRONMENT: needs a TeX Live toolchain; fails with `latexmk: command not found`. Not a code defect and not a broken test. Its second case is also misnamed — execFileSync is synchronous, so the two builds run in sequence, not concurrently.
quarantined.fix: Run on a TeX-provisioned runner, or add a tool guard that skips loudly when latexmk is absent.

$findings: Two REAL subject defects surfaced by the quarantined tests. They are not fixed here and
every failure path into a fallback: an empty source set yields the last HEAD commit,
then the constant 1700000000. A paper whose sources resolve to nothing (a typo'd or
moved filename) still produces a plausible epoch and a confidently reproducible-looking
PDF. The script's stated purpose is catching published-PDF drift; a silent fallback is
how drift gets stamped as authoritative.
2. build-script-not-a-dependency — --changed-since computes per-paper TeX dependency sets
but never treats build-whitepapers.sh itself as a dependency of any paper, so editing
the renderer invalidates no PDF at all.
Also worth a one-line fix by whoever owns the follow-up: three of these files reference
source is spawn-to-person.tex; only the output PDF carries the -whitepaper suffix.
